newsitem.title: UK: Ivory Coast favours keeping ACPC quotas.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast favours keeping ACPC quotas.

text.p: Ivory Coast Commodity Minister Guy- Alain Gauze said at London coffee talks on Wednesday that he favoured retaining a system of export quotas by the Association of Coffee Producing Countries for the six months from July to December.
He was speaking to reporters as delegates gathered for a meeting of the 14-nation ACPC which will decide policy for the second half of 1997.

Delegates said on Monday that an ACPC technical group led by Brazil had proposed that Wednesday's full meeting should adopt a draft plan that would retain quotas but try to make them more flexible, in view of the present volatility in the international market.
Asked about this, however, Gauze said that any introduction of a price trigger mechanism as a basis for quota adjustments would have to wait until "after December".
Gauze was asked whether, at current prices, the ACPC should leave the market alone.
"You mean for the time being, we leave the market to do what it wants to do? I am going to propose to keep the quotas beyond June for the next six months," he said.
He said he wanted quota volumes to be the same as now - the ACPC has a theoretical total export limit of 25.5 million bags - and to apply to both robusta and arabica beans.
Gauze said that an Ivory Coast initiative to tighten curbs on exports earlier in the year was a factor in the present price rally.
"The producers were correct to do what they had done in January. That was the only way for us to succeed and try to push the market up... I did it on behalf of the African producers", he said.
The ACPC meeting began in London's mid-morning.
Delegates could not say when the talks might reach a decision but they doubted if they would get much beyond a secretariat briefing on the state of the market before a lunch adjournment.
Previous ACPC meetings have lasted late into the evening.
The ACPC is meeting in the margin of a week of discussions of the producer/consumer International Coffee Organization (ICO).
Wednesday's ICO diary is thin expect for an informal meeting during the afternoon among private sector participants from both consumers and producers.
